title: Amendment of Class D Airspace and Establishment of Class E2 Airspace Over Hampton, VA
summary:
The government finalized two practical updates: new airspace procedures over Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, Virginia, and a correction to rules for reporting new foreign investment in the United States.

For Hampton, the Federal Aviation Administration is adjusting controlled airspace because the base’s control tower will operate part-time. When the tower is open, the usual close-in control area applies; when it’s closed, a surface-level controlled area will switch on to keep instrument flights orderly and safe. The agency also corrected the official location name to “Hampton, VA” and updated the base’s coordinates. These changes take effect January 22, 2026, and are described as routine, with no significant economic or environmental impacts.

Who benefits? Pilots, air traffic teams, and the local community should see more consistent, predictable handling of flights, especially in bad weather or low visibility. Military operations and nearby airports also gain clarity on who’s in charge and when. Who might be inconvenienced? Some general aviation pilots and flight schools may need to adjust habits, check notices more closely for tower hours, and brief students on the switch between control setups. There may be a short learning curve, but the agency expects minimal disruption.

In related aviation housekeeping, the agency also locked in reference materials and contacts for a separate aircraft safety directive, pointing operators to approved processes and European safety notices now formally incorporated into U.S. guidance. That adds clarity for airlines and maintenance providers, though it can mean extra steps to align with the updated instructions.

Separately, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis issued a correction to its rule for the Survey of New Foreign Direct Investment. The fix clarifies the regulatory instructions and corrects the estimated time to complete a short filing from 36 minutes to 15 minutes. This takes effect October 3, 2025. Companies that report new foreign investment should benefit from clearer directions and a more realistic burden estimate, while compliance teams will want to update internal checklists to reflect the changes.
